title: The normalized free simplex has a natural chain coalgebra diagonal
statement:
Fix a commutative ring $\Lambda$ and the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use simplices and monotone maps as in [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], chain complexes as in [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology], and module tensors as in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For $n\geq0$, let $P(n)_r$ be the free $\Lambda$-module on the strictly increasing strings $0\leq i_0<\cdots<i_r\leq n$ for $r\geq0$, zero otherwise. Its differential is $\partial[i_0,\ldots,i_r]=\sum_{j=0}^{r}(-1)^j[i_0,\ldots,\widehat i_j,\ldots,i_r]$ for $r>0$, zero for $r=0$. For a monotone $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, $P(\alpha)$ sends a basis string to its image string if the images are distinct and to zero otherwise. Let $F(n)$ be the simplicial module whose degree $r$ term is the free module on the monotone maps $[r]\to[n]$, with operators given by precomposition [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. With $N$ as in [lem-cbc-dold-kan-normalization-equivalence], the map $q_n:N(F(n))\to P(n)$ which discards all noninjective basis strings is a natural isomorphism of chain complexes.

The maps
$$D_n[i_0,\ldots,i_r]=\sum_{a=0}^{r}[i_0,\ldots,i_a]\otimes[i_a,\ldots,i_r],\qquad \epsilon_n[i]=1,$$
with $\epsilon_n$ zero in positive degrees, are chain maps $D_n:P(n)\to P(n)\otimes_\Lambda P(n)$ and $\epsilon_n:P(n)\to\Lambda[0]$. Here $(C\otimes C')_r=\bigoplus_{a+b=r}C_a\otimes C'_b$ and $\partial(c\otimes c')=\partial c\otimes c'+(-1)^a c\otimes\partial c'$ for $c\in C_a$. They satisfy $(D_n\otimes\mathrm{id})D_n=(\mathrm{id}\otimes D_n)D_n$ and $(\epsilon_n\otimes\mathrm{id})D_n=\mathrm{id}=(\mathrm{id}\otimes\epsilon_n)D_n$, under the canonical tensor identifications. Every $P(\alpha)$ commutes with $D$ and $\epsilon$.

source.place: Higher Algebra (2017), Remark 1.2.3.16 (kernel and quotient normalization), Construction 1.2.3.22, Remarks 1.2.3.24–25, Example 1.2.3.26 (Alexander–Whitney, naturality and associativity), specialized to free simplices and their diagonal, printed pp.58–64. Read online 2026-10-17; archive WANTED. Stacks Tag 017V, simplicial.tex lemma-splitting-abelian-category, supplies the normalized/degenerate splitting, not the Alexander–Whitney theorem.
